about: Traditional palmistry meanings, summarised in our own short words from two public-domain books. Each entry says which book and chapter it comes from. Meanings that predict health, length of life, accidents, marriage, children, money or crime are deliberately left out (see left_out).

labels.Experimental measurement: A number the AI measured from the 21 hand points. It is real geometry, but the AI's points are joints, not skin creases, and tilting the hand changes it.
labels.Traditional interpretation: What an old palmistry book says this feature means. It is cultural literature, not tested science.
labels.Low confidence: A traditional meaning matched to your hand in a shaky way: the measurement was close to the cut-off, or the book judged this feature by eye in a way the AI cannot copy.

cheiro.author: Cheiro (William John Warner, 1866-1936)
cheiro.title: Palmistry for All
cheiro.note: Part I covers the lines of the palm; Part II (Cheirognomy) covers the shape of the hand, thumb and fingers.

dale.author: Mrs. J. B. Dale
dale.title: Indian Palmistry
dale.tradition: Indian palmistry as retold for English readers, mixed with older European writers (Rothman, Wharton)
dale.note: Dale says a palm can only be read for one or two years ahead, and that palmistry only works together with astrology.

left_out.detail: Both books say the life line (and Dale also the head line) shows how long a person will live and which illnesses they will get. There is no evidence for this. A short life line does not mean a short life.
Cheiro has a whole chapter on 'signs relating to marriage', and Dale counts marks on the side of the hand as 'the number of wives' and children. Not included.
Both books link some marks to accidents, violence or worse. Not included - they are frightening and untested.
Many entries promise riches or warn of ruin. Not included.

Cheiro ranks hand shapes from 'lowest' to 'highest' and ties them to race and class; both books say harsh things about short thumbs and short fingers. Old books carry the prejudices of their time, so these are not repeated.

lines.name: Heart line
lines.where: The top one of the three big creases: it runs across the palm just under the fingers, starting at the little-finger side.

names.dale: Table line, which Dale also calls the 'line of Fortune' (she says the English call it the Heart line)

options.label: Long - reaches under the index finger
Short - stops under the middle finger

questions.text: Where does it end, at the index-finger side?

lines.name: Head line
lines.where: The middle crease: it starts near the thumb side, between thumb and index finger, and runs across the palm.

names.dale: Liver line or 'natural mean' (Dale's 'line of the Head and Brain' is a different, smaller line)

questions.text: Where it starts, does it touch the life line?

lines.name: Life line
lines.where: The curved crease that swings around the base of the thumb.

names.dale: Line of Life - though Dale says it 'ought to be called the line of the Heart'

options.label: A wide curve out into the palm
Faint or made of little pieces

lines.name: Fate line
lines.where: A crease running UP the middle of the palm towards the middle finger. Many people have a faint one, or none.

names.dale: Line of Saturn - which Dale ALSO calls the 'line of Fortune', the same name she gives the heart line

options.label: From the little-finger side of the palm
Only from the middle of the palm
All the way up to the middle finger
Yes - two lines side by side

entries.relation_note: The two books do not even agree what this line is about: for Cheiro it shows the feelings, for Dale it shows steadiness.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. VII 'The Line of Heart'
readings.text: Cheiro read a very long heart line as feelings that run strong and deep - and warned that such strong feelings can tip over into jealousy.

readings.where: 'The Line of Fortune' (her Table line)
readings.text: Dale read a long, unbroken Table line as constancy: someone steady and dependable.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. VII 'The Line of Heart'
readings.text: Cheiro wrote that the shorter the heart line, the less a person shows tender, sentimental feelings - someone who keeps their feelings to themselves.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. VII 'The Line of Heart'
readings.text: Cheiro said the heart line 'should be deep, clear, and well coloured' - his picture of a warm and affectionate nature.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. VII 'The Line of Heart'
readings.meaning: a cool, easy-going attitude to feelings
readings.text: Cheiro linked a pale, shallow heart line with a cooler, more easy-going attitude to feelings.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. VII 'The Line of Heart'
readings.text: Rising from the middle of the mound under the index finger, Cheiro said, shows someone loyal and idealistic, firm in their affections and with a high sense of honour.

entries.variation: ends between index and middle finger

readings.where: Part I, Ch. VII 'The Line of Heart'
readings.text: Cheiro described a calm but very deep nature: not showy, but ready to do a great deal for the people they care about.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. VII 'The Line of Heart'
readings.text: Cheiro read this as a reserved, undemonstrative nature in matters of affection.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. VII 'The Line of Heart'
readings.text: A fork with one branch under the index finger and one between the first two fingers was, for Cheiro, the sign of a well-balanced, happy and affectionate disposition.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. II 'The Line of Head'
readings.text: Cheiro called a head line lying straight across the palm 'level-headed': practical and logical, someone who plans with facts.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. II 'The Line of Head'
readings.text: A gentle downward curve, Cheiro wrote, shows imagination that a person uses when they choose to - he found it often on the hands of artists and painters.

entries.relation_note: Same feature, opposite flavour: careful and unsure of themselves (Cheiro) or quick-witted and even-tempered (Dale).

readings.where: Part I, Ch. II 'The Line of Head joined to the Line of Life'
readings.text: Cheiro read it as a sensitive, careful person who tends to underrate their own talents.

readings.where: 'The Line of Life'
readings.text: Dale read a life line meeting the Liver (head) line in a neat angle as good wit and an even temper - a sharp, quick person.

entries.relation_note: Dale's book reads a separated start completely differently, as a claim about family and marriage that this app does not repeat.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. II 'The Line of Head separated from the Line of Life'
readings.text: A small gap at the start meant, for Cheiro, independent thinking, quick judgement and a certain daring - people who do best when they have a clear purpose.

entries.relation_note: Both books see a clear head line as a good sign, but for different qualities.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. II 'The Line of Head'
readings.text: Cheiro said a clean, deep, thin head line shows strong concentration, and that great 'brain workers' usually have one.

readings.where: 'The Liver Line'
readings.text: Dale wrote that a well-drawn Liver line of a good clear colour is the sign of a cheerful and ingenious disposition.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. II 'The Line of Head'
readings.text: Cheiro thought a broad, shallow head line meant a mind that likes to change direction rather than stay on one track.

entries.relation_note: Dale reads a fork towards the little-finger side as a bad sign, so the two books clash here. Her meaning is not repeated.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. II 'The Line of Head'
readings.text: Cheiro saw a forked head line as a mind balanced between the practical and the imaginative - and advised such people to trust their first impulse instead of weighing both sides for too long.

entries.withheld_note: Dale ties the length of her Liver (head) line to the length of life. This app never repeats that, and there is no evidence for it.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. III 'The Line of Life'
readings.text: A life line sweeping in a wide curve out into the palm was, for Cheiro, a sign of strong energy and warmth towards people.

entries.withheld_note: Cheiro links this curve to a person's health. This app leaves that out.

entries.relation_note: The books disagree on which kind of life line is 'better': Cheiro prefers thin and deep, Dale prefers broad. Dale's reason is about health, so it is not repeated.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. III 'The Line of Life'
readings.text: Cheiro valued a thin, deep, clear life line above a broad one: to him it showed nerve and will-power rather than muscle.

entries.relation_note: Dale thinks a broad life line is the best kind; Cheiro thinks a thin, deep one is better. Dale's reason is about health, so it is not repeated.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. III 'The Line of Life'
readings.text: Cheiro read a broad life line as more physical, muscular strength than will-power - someone at home in an active, outdoor life.

entries.withheld_note: Both books read a faint or broken life line as a health warning. This app leaves that out. A faint line is just a faint crease.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. III 'The Line of Life'
readings.text: A life line starting high, near the index finger, meant to Cheiro more self-control and a life guided by ambition.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. III 'The Line of Life'
readings.text: Cheiro thought a life line starting lower, nearer the thumb, went with less control over the temper.

entries.withheld_note: Both books claim the life line's length shows how long a person will live. That is not true, and this app never says it. A short life line does NOT mean a short life.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. V 'The Line of Destiny or Fate'
readings.text: Cheiro liked a fate line that is clear and distinct but not too heavy - a person with a clear sense of where they are going.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. V 'The Line of Destiny or Fate'
readings.text: A very faint fate line, said Cheiro, belongs to people who do not believe in fate at all - they make their own way with their own minds.

entries.withheld_note: Both books are gloomy about a missing fate line. This app leaves that out - lots of people have no clear fate line at all.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. V 'Rising from the Line of Life'
readings.text: Cheiro read a fate line growing out of the life line as someone who wins things by their own effort and merit, not by luck.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. V 'Rising from the Wrist'
readings.text: A fate line running straight up from the wrist was, for Cheiro, the sign of a smooth and well-favoured path through life - especially, he said, when a clear Sun line goes with it.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. V 'Rising from the Mount of the Moon'
readings.text: Starting from the little-finger side (the 'Mount of the Moon'), Cheiro said, a fate line shows an eventful, changing path, shaped a lot by the people around you.

readings.where: Part I, Ch. V 'Rising from the Middle of the Palm'
readings.text: A fate line that only begins in the middle of the palm meant, for Cheiro, a hard-working person who builds their own success step by step.

readings.where: 'The Line of Saturn'
readings.text: Dale wrote that a Saturn (fate) line running all the way up to the middle finger shows deep thinking and good judgement in giving advice.

entries.withheld_note: Dale calls a short Saturn line a sign of misfortune. This app leaves that out.

entries.relation_note: Same mark, two different stories: two careers (Cheiro) or helping others more than yourself (Dale).

readings.where: Part I, Ch. V 'Double Lines of Fate'
readings.text: Cheiro read a clearly double fate line as two careers carried on together - perhaps one main one and one hobby.

readings.where: 'The Lines' (line of Fortune or Saturn)
readings.text: Dale wrote that when this line doubles in the middle of the palm, 'you do more good to others than yourself'.

readings.where: Part II, Ch. I 'The Square Type'
readings.text: Cheiro's 'square' hand, with a palm about as wide as it is long, belongs to practical, logical people - careful, methodical workers who believe things when they see proof.

entries.stretch: Cheiro sorts long hands into several types using knotty joints and pointed or square fingertips, which the AI cannot see.

readings.where: Part II, Ch. I 'The Philosophic Hand' and 'The Conic or Artistic Hand'
readings.text: In Cheiro's book, long hands belong to the studious 'philosophic' type and the artistic 'conic' type - people drawn to books, ideas, music and beautiful things.

readings.where: Part II, Ch. III 'The Fingers'
readings.text: Cheiro wrote that fingers long in proportion to the palm show a love of thinking and ideas.

entries.stretch: Dale speaks of short hands; the AI measures finger length against the palm.
entries.relation_note: Cheiro was harsh about short fingers; Dale was kinder. Cheiro's view is not repeated.

readings.where: 'A Summary of Judgment'
readings.text: Dale wrote that short hands go with quick judgement - deciding on instinct rather than long analysis.

entries.stretch: Cheiro compared how far the fingertips reach; the AI measures each finger from its knuckle joint.

readings.where: Part II, Ch. III 'The Fingers'
readings.text: Cheiro called the index finger the 'finger of Jupiter': when long, it shows someone who likes to lead and take charge.

entries.stretch: Cheiro compared how far the fingertips reach; the AI measures each finger from its knuckle joint.

readings.where: Part II, Ch. III 'The Fingers'
readings.text: Cheiro called the ring finger the 'finger of the Sun': when long, it shows a love of beautiful things and art - and a wish to be noticed for it.

entries.stretch: Cheiro judged the thumb's length by eye, mostly its top part; the AI measures the whole thumb from its base joint.

readings.where: Part II, Ch. II 'The Thumb'
readings.text: For Cheiro the thumb stands for will-power: the longer it is, the stronger the will.

entries.withheld_note: Cheiro writes very harshly about short thumbs. That is prejudice, not knowledge, so it is not repeated.

entries.measure_label: angle between thumb and index finger (degrees)
entries.relation_note: One feature, two meanings: independence (Cheiro) or generosity (Dale).

readings.where: Part II, Ch. III 'The Fingers'
readings.text: Cheiro wrote that a wide space between thumb and index finger shows independence of will and fearlessness.

readings.where: 'A Summary of Judgment'
readings.text: Dale wrote that a thumb leaning outwards, away from the hand, shows generosity.

entries.feature: Gap between index and middle finger
entries.measure_label: angle between index and middle finger (degrees)

readings.where: Part II, Ch. III 'The Fingers'
readings.text: Cheiro: a wide space between the first and second fingers shows independence of thought.

readings.where: 'A Summary of Judgment'
readings.text: Dale: when the open hand shows the first and second fingers far apart, it 'denotes independence of thought'.

entries.feature: Gap between ring and little finger
entries.measure_label: angle between ring and little finger (degrees)

readings.where: Part II, Ch. III 'The Fingers'
readings.text: Cheiro: a wide space between the third and fourth fingers shows independence of action.

readings.where: 'A Summary of Judgment'
readings.text: Dale agrees: a wide gap here means independence of action - and if both gaps are wide, originality and self-reliance.
